data.content_ref: inline:The target asserts that the cross-city gap is larger in arid regions, but this is backwards for the dominant nocturnal UHI mechanism (stored heat release). In truly arid climates, the rural surroundings are also dry with little evapotranspiration, so the urban–rural latent-heat differential the target relies on is minimized. The strongest nocturnal UHI is typically found in cities with high building/thermal mass AND a surrounding countryside that cools rapidly at night; aridity alone does not maximize the rural moisture advantage, since rural arid sites lack vegetation/irrigation too. The target's single mechanism (reduced evapotranspiration) cannot explain why many high-UHI cities are in humid temperate climates with abundant rural moisture, nor does it address thermal storage as the primary cause of slow nighttime cooling.
